notable_absence.finding: This 233-line page discusses certificate expiration (with a configurable alert period, default 30 days) and manual replacement/rotation, but never once mentions certificate revocation, a CRL (Certificate Revocation List), or OCSP. The only stated way a trusted-but-compromised certificate stops being trusted before its expiration date is deleting the signing CA from the trust store (and only once no node still relies on it) - there is no mechanism described for revoking a single certificate in isolation. Given this page is the corpus's first-ever treatment of certificates, this is a first-order gap in the ontology's coverage of the PKI lifecycle, not just of this page's prose.

cross_component_finding: The page states 'Managing certificates requires the Full Admin or Security Admin roles' without ever naming 'Security Admin' again or linking it to a role reference page. The registry already holds role:full-administrator and role:local-user-security-administrator, both noted (from earlier Capella-side rounds) as gating audit-service configuration specifically. Whether this page's bare 'Security Admin' is the same role as the promoted local-user-security-administrator, a different classic role entirely, or a Capella-only role bleeding into server/ prose, cannot be determined from this page alone - minted separately as role:security-administrator per the project's no-silent-merge rule, flagged for SME/reconciliation review.
cross_product_finding: The Examples section closes with 'They also support secure access to Couchbase Server from Java clients' - naming one specific SDK by name with no link to the Java SDK's own certificate/TLS configuration docs, and no equivalent sentence for any other SDK language. This is a concrete, fixable documentation gap (a missing cross-product xref) rather than a modeling finding, worth a docs-issue in its own right even though this agent is not writing to docs-issues/.
